title: Cordial on-device JSON files
description: JSON documents stored in LittleFS. Each file definition names its path. Select its #/$defs/<name> fragment for a known file. Numeric directory names are positive decimal IDs without prefixes or padding. Device and profile IDs have separate allocation sequences. Enumerated values are stored by name. Temporary .tmp replacements have the destination schema. See storage-format.md for allocation and recovery.
$comment: These schemas describe persisted fields, defaults and structural constraints. Descriptions identify additional firmware validation, including relationships between fields and files. They are documentation, not a replacement for firmware validation. JSON Schema defaults are annotations and do not insert missing fields. Unknown fields are forbidden where the Rust document uses deny_unknown_fields; other objects permit them.

initialized.description: Whether identity roots and the initial sequence have been committed.

address.description: Hexadecimal bytes. Writers use lowercase; readers accept either case.

ir.description: Hexadecimal bytes. Writers use lowercase; readers accept either case.

er.description: Hexadecimal bytes. Writers use lowercase; readers accept either case.

irk.description: Hexadecimal bytes. Writers use lowercase; readers accept either case.

identity.title: /identity.json
identity.description: Adapter Bluetooth identity. The address must match the adapter address. Firmware verifies that IRK equals AES-128 under IR of the 16-byte block ending in 01 with all preceding bytes zero. Cryptographic keys use most-significant byte first.

anyOf.description: Trimmed name with no control characters. Firmware limits UTF-8 encoding to 64 bytes and rejects leading or trailing Unicode whitespace.

name.description: Missing or null selects the board default name. Writers include null.

transports.description: Enabled transports. Empty disables both. Writers list classic before ble and omit duplicates; readers accept duplicates.

configuration_interfaces.description: Saved configuration interface preferences, at most one entry per interface. An interface without an entry is disabled with no profile; writers omit such entries. Firmware refuses to save interfaces it cannot enable together.

adapter.title: /adapter.json
adapter.description: Adapter preferences. If the file is absent, use the board default name, Linux, BLE alone and no configuration interface.

sequence.title: /sequence.json
sequence.description: Last allocated device and profile IDs. Both start at zero. Each allocation increments and saves its counter before publishing a record; deleted IDs are never reused.

device.title: /devices/<id>/device.json
device.description: Paired device policy and complete bond. The decimal directory ID, policy.id and bond.owner must match and be nonzero; policy.peer must equal bond.identity. Device IDs and peer identities must be unique across saved records.

maps.description: Raw HID report descriptors as hex, one per service, each 1..2048 bytes. Writers use lowercase.

reports.description: BLE report characteristics. Omitted when empty.

anyOf.description: Hexadecimal bytes. Writers use lowercase; readers accept either case.

hash.description: Optional GATT Database Hash. Omitted when absent.

layout.title: /devices/<id>/layout.json
layout.description: Optional discovery cache. Classic requires exactly one map and no reports. BLE requires at least one input report. Each report service must index maps; service/kind/id tuples must be unique. An unusable cache is removed and the device is rediscovered.

name.description: Device name. Firmware limits UTF-8 encoding to 128 bytes and excludes ASCII control bytes.

setup_pending.description: True until first-connection setup completes. Writers omit false.

integrations.description: Saved integration preferences, at most one entry per kind.

roles.description: Input roles of the last HID descriptor read. Empty until the first descriptor is read. Writers omit duplicates.

profiles.description: The device's layers: profile IDs applied in order. Absent means an empty list, which passes all input through; writers omit it then. A new device has none.

address.description: Six address bytes in canonical order, unlike the hex string in identity.json.

peer.description: A Classic peer must have random=false. BLE records retain the resolved identity address and address type.

key.description: Hexadecimal bytes. Writers use lowercase; readers accept either case.

bond.description: The externally tagged key variant must match identity.transport. BLE requires an LTK-present flag in local or peer security. A Classic identity cannot use a random address.

flags.description: Bits 0..5: LTK present, IRK present, CSRK present, authenticated, authorized, secure connections.

key_size.description: Must be 7..16 when flags bit 0 indicates an LTK.

rand.description: Hexadecimal bytes. Writers use lowercase; readers accept either case.

ltk.description: Hexadecimal bytes. Writers use lowercase; readers accept either case.

irk.description: Hexadecimal bytes. Writers use lowercase; readers accept either case.

csrk.description: Hexadecimal bytes. Writers use lowercase; readers accept either case.

preference.description: value is numeric: booleans use 0/1; enums use their zero-based enum_values index except wheel.mode, which starts at 1. Nonempty choices must contain value. Otherwise booleans accept 0/1 and integers require a range with value=min+n*step within min..max. See compact::Preference::valid and settings::SettingMetadata::valid for feature/revision, scope and setting-specific constraints.

feature.description: Stable HID++ feature ID, not its device-assigned index.

metadata.description: range may be missing or null. Writers include null. The key must support writes for this feature and revision; report-only keys cannot be saved preferences. Current-host scope is required for multi-host Fn inversion and multi-platform features; other features require device scope. Nonempty choices exclude a range; enums require choices. Integer settings without choices require a range. Boolean settings use neither choices nor a range.

range.description: Inclusive range. max must be at least min and max-min must be divisible by step. Firmware also checks limits specific to each setting.

cccd.description: CCCD handle, omitted when zero. A nonzero handle must exceed value.

name.description: 1..64 UTF-8 bytes without control characters. Whitespace is allowed.

roles.description: The roles the profile's rules change, worked out by firmware whenever the rules are saved.

profile.title: /profiles/<id>/profile.json
profile.description: Profile record. The directory supplies its ID. Publication of this file commits creation; its deletion commits removal.

settings.title: /devices/<id>/settings.json
settings.description: Explicit physical-device preferences, identified by integration and metadata.key. Only hidpp is implemented. Each integration/key pair occurs once. Saving an empty list deletes the file.

layers.description: Profile IDs applied in order. Firmware limits the length to the advertised maximum number of layers. An ID may appear more than once.

remap.description: Outputs held together while the input is held, each at most once. Empty disables the input. Each output names its report collection.

scale.description: [numerator, denominator]; the value is multiplied by numerator/denominator. A negative numerator inverts it.

rules.description: Sorted by input; each input at most once. A rule never remaps its input to only itself in the collection the input arrives in, or scales it by a ratio equal to 1. Output collections are always resolved. Firmware enforces advertised input and output ranges, output counts and the memory budget when saving; it loads saved rules beyond them, and a rule whose input or output it does not support has no effect.

rules.title: /profiles/<id>/rules.json
rules.description: Everything input translation reads for the profile. Absent means no rules. Forgetting the last rule deletes the file.
